name: choice-policy-long
state: 1. Scope: this policy covers every refund, replacement and credit issued to retail customers in the European Economic Area. 2. Refund window: a refund may be issued within 30 calendar days of delivery, counted from the carrier's delivery scan rather than the order date. 3. Proof of purchase: a receipt, invoice number or bank statement is sufficient proof of purchase; a loyalty card number alone is not. 4. Damaged goods: goods damaged in transit are replaced at no cost when the customer reports the damage within 48 hours and provides a photo of the parcel and the item. 5. Opened goods: opened goods may be returned within 14 days when they are unused apart from a reasonable inspection. 6. Hygiene items: opened hygiene items, including milk frothers with a used food contact surface, cannot be returned unless they are faulty. 7. Faulty goods: a fault that appears within six months is presumed to have existed at delivery unless the merchant can show otherwise. 8. Repair first: for goods with a purchase price above 400 EUR the merchant may choose one repair attempt before a replacement is issued. 9. Replacement stock: a replacement is offered from the same warehouse when stock is available, otherwise from any warehouse within the same country. 10. Refund method: refunds go to the original payment method; a cash refund is allowed only when the original payment was cash on delivery. 11. Refund timing: the refund is released within five business days of the returned goods being scanned at the depot, and the payment provider may need another five days. 12. Shipping fees: standard shipping is refunded when the entire order is returned; express surcharges are refunded only when the return is caused by the merchant. 13. Partial returns: when part of an order is returned, a free-shipping threshold granted by the original order is recalculated and the difference may be deducted. 14. Discounts: a discount larger than 20 percent of the order value requires written approval from a finance team lead before it is applied. 15. Credits: a credit note must show the same VAT rate as the invoice it corrects, even when it is issued in a later fiscal quarter. 16. Chargebacks: once a card chargeback is filed, the case moves to the payments team and the customer receives no direct refund until the dispute is closed. 17. Duplicate charges: a duplicate authorization is cancelled immediately when it has not settled; a settled duplicate is refunded with a credit note. 18. Subscription changes: a plan change takes effect at the start of the next billing cycle unless a prorated credit is approved by billing. 19. Price errors: an invoice issued from a stale price book is corrected with a prorated credit within one billing cycle. 20. Reminders: no reminder may be sent for an invoice that is already matched to a payment in the accounting system. 21. Data retention: order records are kept for 24 months after the end of the fiscal year in which the order was fulfilled. 22. Customer records: a deletion request removes the contact record within 30 days but keeps anonymised order lines for the retention period. 23. Access control: only staff with the billing role may view full card numbers; the support role sees the last four digits. 24. Security incidents: a suspected data breach is reported to the security team within 24 hours of discovery, and to the regulator within 72 hours. 25. Passwords: shared support accounts are forbidden; every agent uses a personal account with multi-factor authentication. 26. Escalation: a case older than ten business days without customer contact is escalated to the team lead automatically. 27. Duplicate cases: when two tickets describe the same order and the same fault, the newer ticket is merged into the older one. 28. Language: a customer writing in a language the agent does not speak is routed to the shared language queue instead of being answered with machine translation. 29. Recording: calls are recorded only with an announcement at the start; records are deleted after six months. 30. Concessions: a goodwill gesture above 50 EUR needs a documented reason in the case notes. 31. Warranty: the statutory warranty period of two years applies to every product; the commercial guarantee does not replace it. 32. Return shipping: the merchant pays return shipping for faulty and transit-damaged goods; the customer pays for change-of-mind returns unless the order value exceeds 200 EUR. 33. Inspection: returned goods are inspected at the depot within two business days; the inspection result is recorded against the RMA number. 34. Missing parts: a missing accessory is shipped separately at no cost and does not require a full return. 35. Packaging errors: a repeated packaging error affecting more than five orders is reported as a supplier quality case. 36. Tax: tax corrections are issued by finance only; support agents do not change VAT lines on invoices. 37. Fraud: an order flagged by the fraud screen is held, never cancelled, until the payments team clears it. 38. Address changes: a shipping address may be changed until the order is handed to the carrier; afterwards the customer must wait for delivery and redirect the parcel. 39. Delivery windows: a missed delivery window caused by the carrier is compensated with a shipping credit, not with a product discount. 40. name: score-risk-policy
state: 1. Scope: this policy covers every refund, replacement and credit issued to retail customers in the European Economic Area. 2. Refund window: a refund may be issued within 30 calendar days of delivery, counted from the carrier's delivery scan rather than the order date. 3. Proof of purchase: a receipt, invoice number or bank statement is sufficient proof of purchase; a loyalty card number alone is not. 4. Damaged goods: goods damaged in transit are replaced at no cost when the customer reports the damage within 48 hours and provides a photo of the parcel and the item. 5. Opened goods: opened goods may be returned within 14 days when they are unused apart from a reasonable inspection. 6. Hygiene items: opened hygiene items, including milk frothers with a used food contact surface, cannot be returned unless they are faulty. 7. Faulty goods: a fault that appears within six months is presumed to have existed at delivery unless the merchant can show otherwise. 8. Repair first: for goods with a purchase price above 400 EUR the merchant may choose one repair attempt before a replacement is issued. 9. Replacement stock: a replacement is offered from the same warehouse when stock is available, otherwise from any warehouse within the same country. 10. Refund method: refunds go to the original payment method; a cash refund is allowed only when the original payment was cash on delivery. 11. Refund timing: the refund is released within five business days of the returned goods being scanned at the depot, and the payment provider may need another five days. 12. Shipping fees: standard shipping is refunded when the entire order is returned; express surcharges are refunded only when the return is caused by the merchant. 13. Partial returns: when part of an order is returned, a free-shipping threshold granted by the original order is recalculated and the difference may be deducted. 14. Discounts: a discount larger than 20 percent of the order value requires written approval from a finance team lead before it is applied. 15. Credits: a credit note must show the same VAT rate as the invoice it corrects, even when it is issued in a later fiscal quarter. 16. Chargebacks: once a card chargeback is filed, the case moves to the payments team and the customer receives no direct refund until the dispute is closed. 17. Duplicate charges: a duplicate authorization is cancelled immediately when it has not settled; a settled duplicate is refunded with a credit note. 18. Subscription changes: a plan change takes effect at the start of the next billing cycle unless a prorated credit is approved by billing. 19. Price errors: an invoice issued from a stale price book is corrected with a prorated credit within one billing cycle. 20. Reminders: no reminder may be sent for an invoice that is already matched to a payment in the accounting system. 21. Data retention: order records are kept for 24 months after the end of the fiscal year in which the order was fulfilled. 22. Customer records: a deletion request removes the contact record within 30 days but keeps anonymised order lines for the retention period. 23. Access control: only staff with the billing role may view full card numbers; the support role sees the last four digits. 24. Security incidents: a suspected data breach is reported to the security team within 24 hours of discovery, and to the regulator within 72 hours. 25. Passwords: shared support accounts are forbidden; every agent uses a personal account with multi-factor authentication. 26. Escalation: a case older than ten business days without customer contact is escalated to the team lead automatically. 27. Duplicate cases: when two tickets describe the same order and the same fault, the newer ticket is merged into the older one. 28. Language: a customer writing in a language the agent does not speak is routed to the shared language queue instead of being answered with machine translation. 29. Recording: calls are recorded only with an announcement at the start; records are deleted after six months. 30. Concessions: a goodwill gesture above 50 EUR needs a documented reason in the case notes. 31. Warranty: the statutory warranty period of two years applies to every product; the commercial guarantee does not replace it. 32. Return shipping: the merchant pays return shipping for faulty and transit-damaged goods; the customer pays for change-of-mind returns unless the order value exceeds 200 EUR. 33. Inspection: returned goods are inspected at the depot within two business days; the inspection result is recorded against the RMA number. 34. Missing parts: a missing accessory is shipped separately at no cost and does not require a full return. 35. Packaging errors: a repeated packaging error affecting more than five orders is reported as a supplier quality case. 36. Tax: tax corrections are issued by finance only; support agents do not change VAT lines on invoices. 37. Fraud: an order flagged by the fraud screen is held, never cancelled, until the payments team clears it. 38. Address changes: a shipping address may be changed until the order is handed to the carrier; afterwards the customer must wait for delivery and redirect the parcel. 39. Delivery windows: a missed delivery window caused by the carrier is compensated with a shipping credit, not with a product discount. 40. Held stock: reserved stock is released after 48 hours when the payment has not been captured. 41. B2B orders: business orders above 2,000 EUR require a signed quote and are excluded from the retail refund window. 42. Promotions: a promotional bundle that is partially returned keeps the bundle price for the retained items and refunds the remainder at bundle rate. 43. Gift cards: gift cards are refunded as a gift card, never as cash, and expire after 36 months. 44. Recalls: a recalled product is refunded in full regardless of the refund window and without requiring the original packaging. 45. Safety: any report of smoke, fire or electric shock is escalated to the safety desk within one hour and the product is quarantined. 46. Documentation: every refund over 100 EUR needs the invoice number in the case notes; every replacement needs the RMA number. 47. Approval matrix: refunds up to 100 EUR are approved by the agent, up to 500 EUR by the team lead, and above 500 EUR by the finance lead. 48. Audit: a random sample of 5 percent of refunds is audited monthly, and every audited case must keep its evidence for 24 months. 49. Complaints: a complaint about a policy decision is answered within three business days with the policy clause that applies. 50. Review: this policy is reviewed twice a year by support, finance and legal, and every change is announced one week before it takes effect. 51. Bundles: a bundle returned in parts keeps the bundle discount only while at least half of the bundle's items are kept. 52. Deposits: a deposit for a custom order is refundable until production starts and non-refundable afterwards unless the merchant cancels. 53. Pre-orders: a pre-order may be cancelled at any time before the release date and is refunded in full within five business days. 54. Shipping damage: a parcel with visible outer damage may be refused at the door, which counts as a transit damage report. 55. Lost parcels: a parcel that has not moved for seven days is treated as lost and replaced or refunded at the customer's choice. 56. Returns abroad: cross-border returns use the merchant's carrier account when the return is caused by the merchant and the customer's account otherwise. 57. Fees: no restocking fee is charged for faulty goods, transit damage or recalls; a restocking fee of up to 10 percent may apply to large appliances returned without cause. 58. Inspection delays: when the depot cannot inspect within two business days, the refund is released on the customer's photos alone. 59. Store credit: store credit is offered only when the customer asks for it and may never replace a refund the customer is entitled to. 60. Price matching: a lower price at another retailer is matched within 14 days of purchase when the competitor has the item in stock. 61. Coupons: an expired coupon is not applied retroactively, but a coupon that expired during a checkout error is honoured manually. 62. Invoices: an invoice is issued at the latest on the day the order ships, never before the payment is captured. 63. Payment capture: a payment is captured only when the order is ready to ship; authorizations older than seven days are released. 64. Three dimensional secure: a payment that fails the second factor twice is not retried automatically and the customer is asked to use another method. 65. Refunds after chargeback: a refund already issued before a chargeback is documented in the dispute file and never repeated. 66. Duplicate refunds: a second refund for the same invoice is blocked by the payment run and reviewed by finance. 67. Customer contact: every case needs at least one attempt to contact the customer within two business days of the first agent reply.
